the Model Predictive Control gives better performance than Linear Quadratic Regulators.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for flexible manipulators and its control using Model Predictive and Linear Quadratic Regulators.
modelling and identification of a flexible link manipulator.
modelling of a flexible robot, identification of its model using fuzzy approach and finally controlling its tip vibration using model predictive control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Model Predictive Control outperforms the Linear Quadratic Regulators in terms of the settling time of the system.
the Model Predictive Control provides better results than the LQR controller and hence can be implemented in the real time system.
the proposed MPC controller has better performance than the LQR controller in terms of settling time, peak overshoot and rise time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Model Predictive Control provides a better performance in terms of settling time and overshoot.
the MPC controller is able to track the desired tip position and the fuzzy controller is able to predict the tip position with high accuracy.
we have designed a flexible manipulator using T S fuzzy identification and Model Predictive Control and compared it with the LQR controller and found the results to be better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can design a controller which can be implemented in a real time system for controlling the flexible manipulator.
MPC is better in controlling the vibration as compared to LQR controller.
MPC is a better controller as compared to LQR and the fuzzy identification is better than the conventional identification methods.
